newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia to earn $57 mln from its shipping line.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia to earn $57 mln from its shipping line.

text.p: Land-locked Ethiopia has forecast earnings of around $57 million in 1996/97 from its 12 cargo ships plying international sea routes, state-owned Ethiopian Shipping Line (ESL) said on Wednesday.
That compared with earnings of $48 million in 1995/96 and $40.9 million in 1994/95 from the ships, it said in a report.
The state-owned shipping line said its 12 ships with aggregate capacity of more than 95,000 tonnes consisted of multi-purpose ships and tankers.
The ships sail to Britain, Western Europe, the Mediterranean and the Adriatic, the Far East, the Gulf and the Red Sea areas.
Although ESL has its headquarters in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa, its ships have as bases the Eritrean Red Sea ports of Assab and Massawa and the port of Djibouti.
Ethiopia became land-locked following the independence of its northern province of Eritrea in 1993.
ESL started operations in 1966 and has played a major role in the growth and expansion of Ethiopia's import and export trade.
